expected_observations.expected_pattern: The effective rate initially tracks m and then bends toward the low-energy support.
expected_observations.what_it_would_teach: Finite-window decay is not enough; the route needs a lower spectral support statement for all non-vacuum excitations.
expected_observations.what_would_disconfirm_it: If the branch can prove the spectral measure has no support below m for a dense observable sector.

failure_modes: The situation is used to argue by analogy instead of localizing a missing lemma.
The branch ignores that tiny tails can dominate late-time behavior.
The follow-up cycle fails to state which observable sector is being tested.

followup_cycle_tasks.description: Derive the exact condition under which Laplace decay bounds imply a spectral support gap for a family of observables.
followup_cycle_tasks.failure_or_demotion_criterion: If the condition only holds for one observable, demote to evidence task.
followup_cycle_tasks.situation_title: A positive spectral measure with hidden low-energy leakage
followup_cycle_tasks.success_criterion: The condition names the observable family, measure support, and large-time uniformity requirement.

insight_hypotheses: A correlator route must formulate a no-low-energy-tail lemma, not only a decay estimate.
Observable density is a decisive bridge premise for turning Euclidean behavior into Hamiltonian spectrum.

interventions.decision_value: Forces the next cycle to ask for uniform asymptotic decay and observable-density control.
interventions.operation: Make epsilon small enough that finite t windows look exponentially gapped.
interventions.predicted_direction: C(t) appears to decay with rate m on bounded windows but is eventually dominated by the low-energy tail.

criteria_met: The branch interprets Euclidean decay as spectral-gap evidence.
A controlled contrast can separate finite-window decay from support bounded away from zero.
criteria_missing: Observable-density and large-time uniformity remain open.
need_assessment.why_not_direct_derivation_or_probe: A direct proof attempt would likely restate the support condition; the imagined leakage situation makes the missing condition visible.

proposed_graph_updates.rationale: Thought experiment identifies low-energy leakage as a required falsifier for decay-to-gap transfer.

situation.controlled_contrast: Compare apparent finite-window exponential decay against true large-t spectral support.
situation.mathematical_carrier: Laplace transform C(t)=int exp(-t lambda) dmu_O(lambda) with a small low-energy tail.
situation.minimal_world: Imagine a positive measure dmu_O(lambda) with most mass above m but a tunable tiny tail near zero.
non_claims: This does not assert that Yang-Mills has low-energy leakage.
This does not produce a spectral theorem proof.
This only isolates the failure mode of finite-window or restricted-observable decay.
situation.purpose: Elicit the difference between decay of one correlator and a gap in the full excitation sector.
situation.title: A positive spectral measure with hidden low-energy leakage
situation.why_this_situation_is_informative: It shows why observable density and uniform long-time control are needed before a correlator estimate becomes a mass-gap witness.

transfer_scope.does_not_transfer: Any actual spectral support claim about the target theory.
transfer_scope.transfer_certificate_needed: OS reconstruction plus a dense gauge-invariant observable sector.
transfer_scope.transfers: The conceptual failure mode of finite-window decay and restricted observable support.

trigger_criteria: The branch interprets Euclidean decay as spectral-gap evidence.
A controlled contrast can separate finite-window decay from support bounded away from zero.

variants.changed_condition: Require the observable algebra to approximate every non-vacuum excitation.
variants.predicted_change: Decay of a sufficiently rich family can become a spectral witness.
variants.reason_for_variant: Separates one-observable decay from sector-wide mass gap evidence.
